vMatrix.notes: Re-verification pass 2026-09-12: every node and trio above was re-read on its cited page and every one matched. Nothing here was fabricated and nothing needed deleting; what changed is the labelling - three consensus labels were downgraded because a source that merely does not contradict a claim was previously being counted as a source that supports it (node 4 grouping, node 6 grouping, and the bossing trio). Grandis Library exposes a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle on class pages, which is direct evidence that boost-node groupings changed at v.269; both independent trio sources (mastermysty 2024-11-21, DigitalTQ 2024-12-04) predate that change, so where they disagree with Grandis the Grandis grouping is the newer one - but Grandis's judgement fields are credited to the Aran Discord, not independently derived. Tier labels: Grandis renders PRIMARY / SECONDARY / OTHER as colour, not text. Its Boost Node Legend defines PRIMARY as 'Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used', SECONDARY as 'Boost Nodes that don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery but are still used', and OTHER as 'Boost Nodes that do not need to be upgraded or has least priority' - that legend text IS extractable and was re-read 2026-09-12, but which node carries which colour is not, so no tier is asserted here. See conflicts for what the legend plus the wiki's HEXA Mastery list implies and why that implication is left as an implication. No public Aran class Google Doc exists - Grandis Library's Other Resources block for Aran lists the Class Discord and wikis and has no Class Doc link, unlike most other classes.

hexa.notes: This is the whole public HEXA picture for Aran and it rests on ONE artifact: a 'Simplified Hexa Matrix' infographic credited in-image to 'Ziby' and linking the Aran Discord (discord.gg/WpJ4VDta8V), republished on Mapler House with a module date of 2026-06-19. Grandis Library has no HEXA section on any class page and no Aran class doc exists, so there is no second opinion available publicly. Extraction caveat (unchanged): the infographic conveys order entirely through 36 skill icons with a target level under each, and two of the node ladders use near-identical blue-and-gold icons that could not be told apart at source resolution - those two ladders (seven cells between them) are deliberately NOT assigned to named nodes. RESOLVED 2026-09-12: the fourth HEXA Mastery core is no longer unknown. MapleStory Wiki's Aran/Skills page lists Core 4 as a choice of HEXA Permafrost, HEXA Adrenaline Overload or HEXA Final Attack; the infographic's ordering advice applies to whichever is chosen, and no source states which to choose. NEW FRESHNESS GAP found 2026-09-12: MapleStory Wiki lists TWO class-specific HEXA skill cores for Aran - Skill Node/Core 1 (Origin) Endgame and Skill Node/Core 2 (Ascent) Hailstorm Howl. The infographic's order covers Endgame only and says nothing about an Ascent core, which is consistent with it predating KMS ver. 1.2.417 (2026-07-31). Whether Hailstorm Howl has reached GMS by v.271 was not established this session - it is recorded as present on the wiki and nothing more. The investment order below Endgame should be treated as incomplete for that reason.

gearingNotes: Sourced class-specific numbers, all from Grandis Library's 'Base Stats (From Skills)' table for Aran: crit rate +55% from class passives, ignore DEF +40% (up to +49.6%), final damage +33.1% (up to +41.09%), damage +65% (up to +95%), boss damage +7% (up to +32%), crit damage +21%, weapon mastery 90%, attack speed Stage 5. The +55% passive crit rate is the figure that should drive how much crit rate an Aran buys from links, legion and hyper stats, and it sits alongside a HEXA Stat priority that puts Crit Damage second behind Attack - but no source explicitly connects those two facts, so the connection is not asserted here. Aran is a straightforward STR/DEX warrior with no unusual resource or stat-conversion mechanic of the Demon Avenger or Xenon kind; nothing found in any source flags a gearing quirk beyond the passive crit rate.
